a paired phone.says: a phone paired with a code, as the pairing page does it (POST /pair); phone requests carry its key as ?t=. A code open before is open after

a T3 hire.says: registry.json holds a hire in T3 Code (engine t3, with its thread and worktree): the Mac gives it a desk at a free key, from the registry alone, with no control (T3D-a); T3 Code isn't asked

messages.text: Please look at the login change first.

messages.note: Kept for the GM to read; not typed into its session.

body.message: Claude needs your permission to use Bash

sessions.says: before its hooks, contract-a's tab (launcher:contract-a) is a hire's, opened with the role reviewer: the Mac keeps that in Deck.hiredTabs, the Go app in its launcher (launcherConnected)

T3 Code on.says: config.json's t3CodeEnabled is true (the T3 Code choice, T796)

the app's briefs.says: the library you edit (the support folder's briefs/templates) is the app's own, Resources/briefs: the Go app has it built in and copies it there on first use; the Mac's test bundle has none, so its test copies it there

the phone mic off.says: config.json's phoneMicEnabled is false (setup's Phone microphone): the Go app reads it too since I5, with no switch for it in setup yet (M2)

note: The Swift engine's answers, written by its ContractTests.swift (gone with it in M7), kept by hand since as the Go app's reference and read by desktop/contract_test.go. Shapes, not values: "string", "number", "bool", "null"; 'x' for that string; alternatives joined by | ("string|null", a closed set 'a'|'b'); an object's keys, no more, no fewer; an array's elements as the different shapes they have, each element like one of them and each like some element ([] for none). "any", "object", "map" (keys are data) and "array" compare no further: INVENTORY.md lists each, with why, and each null allowed. Beside a shape, ids: the given's sessions in each of its lists, sorted, compared as they are; and t3Desk: what every t3: desk must hold by value (each 'false' field false, each 'null' field null, its t3 with each of those fields, no / in a 'noSlash' field). A refusal answered in JSON has its shape too.
